summary:
West Virginia's controlling statute on sex and facilities is Senate Bill 456, the Riley Gaines Act, signed by Governor Patrick Morrisey on 12 March 2025 after passing the state Senate on 3 March and the House of Delegates on 6 March. It defines "woman" as an adult human of the female sex and "man" as an adult human of the male sex, and the law recognises no category beyond male and female; language requiring genital examination was struck before signing. At the ceremony the Governor said bathrooms, locker rooms, domestic violence shelters and rape crisis centres "should be kept private for women only."

The statute's stated reach covers locker rooms, bathrooms, rape crisis centres, dormitories and prisons, so exposure runs from a rest stop restroom to any shelter or correctional setting a visitor might enter. West Virginia's facility restrictions are catalogued in the Movement Advancement Project's equality map of state bans on transgender people's use of public bathrooms and facilities according to their gender identity.

An independent anti-trans legal risk assessment published 27 August 2026 places West Virginia in its "Worst States" group, one tier below the four states it rates "Do Not Travel," within a national frame it describes as "Worst Policies In Effect."

State identity documents remain changeable but the route is narrow. A gender marker on a West Virginia birth certificate requires a Birth Certificate Request Form with a court order for gender change and fees paid to Vital Registration; a driver's licence or state ID requires a Gender Designation Form signed by a licensed physician, with no surgery or sterilisation required. In July 2020 the West Virginia Supreme Court upheld a circuit court's refusal to allow a marker change even after reassignment surgery, so a court order does not guarantee approval.

House Bill 3293, passed in March 2021 and effective 1 July 2021, restricts transgender athletes from teams aligned with their gender identity by defining male and female solely on reproductive biology and genetics at birth. The Fourth Circuit held the ban unconstitutional in West Virginia v. B.P.J. in April 2024, and in July 2025 the Supreme Court agreed to hear the case, leaving the operative position unsettled.

Gender-affirming care for minors is restricted by a March 2023 law effective 1 January 2024 banning puberty blockers, hormone therapy and surgery except for severe dysphoria diagnosed by at least two physicians. For adults, a 1997 Medicaid ban on sexual reassignment surgery was ruled unconstitutional in August 2022 and coverage was required, but the Fourth Circuit overturned that ruling in 2026, holding that refusing funding is not irrational; Anderson v. Crouch, challenging the adult Medicaid exclusion, was argued on 9 December 2025 and remains unresolved.

An April 2025 bill passed both houses and awaited gubernatorial action that would require teachers and principals to immediately out transgender, non-binary and intersex students to parents and guardians.

West Virginia statutes provide no discrimination protection on gender identity, and the only statewide employment protection comes from Bostock v. Clayton County under federal Title VII. Fifteen cities bar gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations, with further protections for county and city employees in Kanawha County, Buckhannon and Elkins. House Bill 3042, passed 27 and 28 February 2023, is a Religious Freedom Restoration Act letting a person or corporation claim that a state or local law or government policy burdens religious belief and claim exemption from compliance, which permits denial of business service, housing and government service on grounds of gender identity, and it carries qualified immunity. On 26 March 2025 the state Senate approved by 25 to 8 a bill to nullify all city and county LGBTQ anti-discrimination ordinances, which awaited a House vote.

Marriage for couples the state would class as same-sex has been recognised since 9 October 2014, when Attorney General Patrick Morrisey ceased defending the ban and Governor Earl Ray Tomblin directed agencies to comply with federal rulings, despite a statute defining marriage as between a man and a woman that was never repealed.
tangentialFactors:
The risk tiering in the August 2026 assessment is comparative rather than statistical: West Virginia sits in the second-highest of five groups, while Idaho was moved up to "Do Not Travel" after enacting a felony bathroom ban carrying up to five years, partially court-blocked but in force wherever no gender-neutral option exists. The tiering reflects what statutes are on the books, not measured rates of incidents against visitors.

The legal position in West Virginia is in motion on several fronts at once. The athletics ban is before the Supreme Court after the Fourth Circuit struck it down, the adult Medicaid exclusion is under active challenge, the local-ordinance nullification bill and the student-outing bill were both passed by one or both chambers and their final disposition is not established in the available sources. A visitor should treat any single provision here as provisional and check its current status before travel.

The Movement Advancement Project page that enumerates West Virginia's facility ban has been moved by the publisher and now returns a 404, so the enumeration is cited from the source inventory rather than verified against the live page.
localsOnly:
Residents change a birth-certificate gender marker through a Birth Certificate Request Form accompanied by a court order for gender change and fees filed with Vital Registration, and change a driver's licence or state ID through a Gender Designation Form signed by a licensed physician, with no surgery or sterilisation required. The July 2020 West Virginia Supreme Court decision upholding a Wood County Circuit Court denial of a marker change even after sexual reassignment surgery shows the court route can fail.

Fifteen cities maintain ordinances barring gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations, and Kanawha County, Buckhannon and Elkins extend protection to county and city employees. These local protections are the only non-discrimination cover available in the state and the March 2025 Senate bill would strip them; the 2023 religious-refusal statute lets a business, landlord or agency refuse service on religious grounds with qualified immunity.

There is no statewide conversion-therapy law. Charleston banned the practice by a 14-9 vote in August 2021 and Morgantown by 7-0 in October 2021, so protection depends on municipal boundaries.

Married same-sex couples may adopt, lesbian couples may access in vitro fertilisation, state law recognises a married non-genetic non-gestational mother after donor insemination, and gestational and traditional surrogacy are valid with equal treatment of different-sex and same-sex couples. Same-sex couples receive hospital visitation through a designated visitor statute.

Employment discrimination on gender identity is addressed only through federal Title VII as construed in Bostock v. Clayton County, effective 15 June 2020, alongside the fifteen city ordinances and the county and town employee policies.
outOfScope:
The Movement Advancement Project equality-map page cited for West Virginia's facility-ban enumeration now returns a 404 after the publisher moved it; the enumeration could not be re-verified against a live page.

The final status of the April 2025 student-outing bill is unresolved. The sources record that it passed both houses and awaited gubernatorial action, with no record of signature or veto.

The status of the March 2025 bill nullifying local non-discrimination ordinances is unresolved beyond Senate approval on 26 March 2025 by 25 to 8; no House vote is sourced.

Anderson v. Crouch was argued on 9 December 2025 and no outcome is sourced. West Virginia v. B.P.J. was accepted by the Supreme Court in July 2025 with no decision recorded here.

No source documents an arrest, prosecution or civil penalty under the Riley Gaines Act, nor any specific refusal of service to a trans visitor under the 2023 religious-refusal statute; enforcement patterns in practice are not sourced.
